AN ACT to amend the executive law, in relation to the discharging of certain
sentences
items.memo:
BILL NUMBER: S5375

SPONSOR: SEPULVEDA
 
TITLE OF BILL:

An act to amend the executive law, in relation to the discharging of
certain sentences

 
PURPOSE OR GENERAL IDEA OF BILL:

This bill will allow those serving indeterminate sentences to be
discharged from parole

 
SUMMARY OF SPECIFIC PROVISIONS:

Amends Subdivision 1 of section 259-j of the Executive law

 
JUSTIFICATION:

Under existing law, individuals on community supervision remain under
supervision until they are discharged from their sentences. If they meet
certain criteria, parolees may be considered for merit termination
termination of their sentence after three years of unrevoked super-
vision. If eligible, their parole officer will submit the case to the
Board Parole, pursuant to Executive Law 259(j) for three-year discharge
consideration.  Otherwise, individuals on community supervision will be
discharged when they have reached the maximum expiration date of their
sentence or they have completed the court imposed period of post-release
supervision.

This bill allows the board of parole to give 3-year parole discharges
for good behavior to everyone, not just those with indeterminate
sentences. Right now an individual who has a life sentence can get
discharged from parole after three years of unrevoked parole however, a
person who has 5 years of community supervision on a flat 10 year bid
has to serve all five years.

 
PRIOR LEGISLATIVE HISTORY:

New bill.

 
FISCAL IMPLICATIONS:

To be determined - should lead to a cost savings for the state.

 
LOCAL FISCAL IMPLICATIONS:

None

 
EFFECTIVE DATE:
This act shall take effect immediately.

summary: Relates to the discharging of certain sentences; makes all felonies eligible for discharge.
